title: Poke
description: One still frame of a tree against a summer sky, from a clip filmed on a tripod in the wind. Twenty-six seconds of its real motion were taken apart into the tree's own vibration modes: twelve shapes, each with the frequency and damping the clip measured, from a slow 0.36 Hz sway of the whole crown to quicker 1.3 Hz shivers in single branches. Take hold of any part of the tree and pull. The spot under your hand follows it, and the rest of the crown answers through the modes it shares with that spot, each part with its own lag. Let go and everything rings down in its own time, coupled the way the real branches are. Nothing about the motion is invented.
intent: Image-Space Modal Bases / Interactive Dynamic Video: Abe Davis, Justin G. Chen and Fredo Durand, 'Image-Space Modal Bases for Plausible Manipulation of Objects in Video', ACM Transactions on Graphics 34(6), SIGGRAPH Asia 2015 (https://dspace.mit.edu/handle/1721.1/137568, https://www.provideocoalition.com/pokemon-go-interactive-dynamic-video/), the method that Generative Image Dynamics (Li, Tucker, Snavely and Holynski, CVPR 2024) drives with a diffusion prior. Here it runs on real footage, as in the original. Offline (tools/depth/bakes/poke): DIS optical flow from a reference frame to all 772 frames, photometrically checked; Frequency Domain Decomposition (Brincker, Zhang and Andersen 2000) of all the motion at once, so every singular vector at a spectral peak is a complex 2D mode shape; the twelve strongest spatially coherent ones kept; frequency and damping from an SDOF fit to each modal coordinate's spectrum; quantised into a 12-layer texture array. Live: complex modal oscillators driven by the hand, a closed-loop spring at the grabbed material point whose force is projected onto the modes (f_i = phi_i(m)^H F); the reference frame is backward-warped by the sum of the modes, with the tree matted over a filled, regraded sky so a branch that swings away uncovers sky. Developed through the lab film kit (summer). Patent note: MIT holds a patent on this method (Davis et al., image-space modal bases / interactive dynamic video). This is a non-commercial portfolio reimplementation of the published paper; clear it before any commercial use. Stills: ?poke=x,y,amp[,deg]&t=seconds (print uv, pull as a fraction of the print's width toward deg, default left; t after letting go, omit to hold), ?still=1 stops the breeze.

sources.author: Engin Akyurt (https://www.pexels.com/@enginakyurt/)
sources.note: 1920x1080, 29.97 fps, 25.8 s, locked off on a tripod. Reference frame 382 (the frame closest to the clip's mean pose). Flow with OpenCV DIS at 960x540, modal grid 320x180. Tree matted off the sky by colour and a guided filter; sky behind filled by push-pull and regraded toward the genre's cobalt (polariser-like, deeper at the top).
